intro.title: Discover Letná Park
intro.equivalenceStatement: Letná Park — in Czech Letenské sady — is the terraced park on the Letná plateau above the Vltava in Prague 7. The large open ground immediately west of it, Letenská pláň, is a separate flat area used for sport, markets and open-air concerts; most visitors experience the two as one continuous Letná area.
intro.description:
Letná Park occupies the clifftop edge of the Letná plateau on the left bank of the Vltava, looking across the river towards the Old Town bridges, Petřín Hill and Prague Castle. Because the park sits roughly 40 metres above the water, its terraces deliver the classic postcard view of Prague without a ticket, a lift or a queue.

The green space itself is a grid of shaded allées, open lawns and promenades: locals picnic on the grass, runners use the flat paths along the ridge and families head for the playgrounds near Letenské náměstí. On the eastern edge stands Letná Beer Garden, whose terrace shares the same panorama as the viewpoint.

Two landmarks anchor the plateau. The Hanavský Pavilion is a cast-iron exhibition hall from the 1891 Jubilee Exhibition. The Metronome, a kinetic sculpture installed in 1991, stands on the plinth left behind by the Stalin Monument that was demolished in 1962. Visiting Letná Park is free at any hour, which is why it is one of the few central viewpoints in Prague that stays accessible after dark.

visitGuide.title: Visit Tips
items: Entry is free and the paths stay open after sunset
Allow 60–90 minutes for viewpoints and the promenade
Arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset if you want space on the terrace
Combine it with a walk downhill to Malá Strana or across Charles Bridge
Spring and autumn give the clearest views; summer haze builds up on hot afternoons

viewpoints.title: Best viewpoints in Letná Park
viewpoints.intro: Four spots on the plateau give noticeably different photographs. Coordinates are approximate — check them against the map below before you set out.

items.name: Beer garden terrace
items.walk: 4 minutes on flat ground from the Letenské náměstí tram stop
items.view: South-east across the Vltava to the Old Town bridge group, with Petřín Hill behind them
items.bestTime: Late afternoon; seating fills up on warm weekends

items.name: Metronome platform
items.walk: 7 minutes from Letenské náměstí, downhill along the ridge
items.view: Wide river bend plus the Prague Castle silhouette to the south
items.bestTime: Blue hour, when the moving arm is lit

items.name: Hanavský Pavilion terrace
items.walk: 5 minutes from Letenské náměstí through the park
items.view: Framed view between trees — good for compressed telephoto shots of the castle
items.bestTime: Morning, when the light falls across the bridges

items.name: Edge of Letenská pláň
items.walk: 10 minutes up from Hradčanská metro station
items.view: Open, elevated horizon over the stadium roof towards the castle district
items.bestTime: Concert-free weekday evenings for empty compositions

viewpoints.note: The terraces face south-east, so the sunset position shifts through the year: in high summer the sun drops to the north-west, behind the viewpoint, while in spring and autumn it sets closer to Prague Castle.

sections.title: Historical Changes
sections.content: The Letná plateau was vineyards and open land outside the city walls before it was planted as public grounds in the 19th century. The largest structure ever built here was the Stalin Monument, unveiled in 1955 and demolished by controlled explosions in 1962. In 1991 the Metronome by sculptor Vratislav Karel Novák was installed on the surviving plinth, deliberately covering the site with something impermanent. Since then the plateau has also been the setting for large public gatherings, including the 1989 demonstrations before the Velvet Revolution and, later, the biggest open-air concerts held in Prague.

sections.title: Landscape Features
sections.content: Letenské sady is laid out for promenading: tree-lined allées run along the ridge, opening onto lawns and onto a paved terrace that follows the retaining wall above the river. The drop of roughly 40 metres from the terrace to the water is what makes the panorama work — you look across, not up. The Hanavský Pavilion, a cast-iron structure from the 1891 Jubilee Exhibition, sits at the eastern end and is the park's only significant built landmark.

sections.title: Cultural Significance
sections.content: For Praguers, Letná is an everyday park rather than a monument: it is used for jogging, picnics, dog walking, skateboarding under the Metronome and Sunday afternoons on the grass. That everyday quality is exactly why the viewpoint is rarely as crowded as Petřín Hill or the Old Town Hall tower, despite being free and visible.

sections.title: Core Experience
sections.content: The most reliable experience is a walk from Letenské náměstí to the terrace in the late afternoon: cross the park, take in successive angles of the bridges, stop at the Metronome, then choose between the beer garden terrace and the open edge of Letenská pláň for sunset. In good weather the whole loop takes about an hour; with a stop for a drink it easily fills an evening.

hours.title: Opening Hours
hours.outdoorTime: Open 24 hours, year-round, free of charge
hours.beerGardenTime: Seasonal, roughly spring to autumn; typically late morning until around 23:00. Closed or limited in winter — check on site.
hours.tip: The terraces stay open after dark; lighting along the allées is moderate, so bring a torch if you are leaving late.

tickets.title: Ticket Prices
tickets.outdoorPrice: Free, no ticket and no reservation
tickets.beerGardenPrice: No admission charge; you pay for what you order
tickets.note: Nothing on the plateau costs an entry fee. Any charge applies only to what you order at the kiosks or beer garden.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.airportDesc: From Václav Havel Airport Prague take trolleybus 59 to Nádraží Veleslavín, then Metro A to Hradčanská and walk up through the park, about 10 minutes to the terrace.
transport.intercityDesc: From Praha hlavní nádraží take Metro C to Muzeum and change to Metro A for Hradčanská, or take tram 26 straight to Letenské náměstí, which drops you almost inside the park.
transport.metroDesc: Metro A to Hradčanská, then about 10 minutes uphill through Letenské sady to the viewpoint. Malostranská (also line A) works if you prefer a short, steeper climb.
transport.tramDesc: Trams 1, 8, 12, 25 and 26 stop at Letenské náměstí — the flatest approach, about 4 minutes from the terrace with no hill to climb.
transport.busDesc: Bus 131 to Sparta is the shortest hop from Holešovice and the stadium side of the plateau.
transport.selfDriveDesc: Driving is the weakest option: parking across Letná is dominated by resident-only blue zones with weekday enforcement. See the parking section below for paid alternatives.
transport.walkingDesc: From the Old Town the walk takes 20–30 minutes across the river and up; from Malá Strana it is a 15–20 minute climb.
transport.cyclingDesc: Shared bikes and bike lanes along the river make cycling a comfortable approach, though the climb from the riverbank is steep in places.
transport.tipsDesc: Tram to Letenské náměstí avoids every hill on the plateau. Buy a Prague public transport ticket before boarding — fines for travelling without validation are common.

parking.title: Parking near Letná Park
parking.intro: Parking is the single most common practical question about this area, and the honest answer is: do not rely on street parking here.
items: Streets across Letná and Holešovice are largely resident-priority blue zones (modré zóny) enforced on weekdays; visitor parking is limited to a few marked bays
The few paid car parks around the stadium and Letenské náměstí fill quickly on sunny weekends and during events on Letenská pláň
A park-and-ride is usually faster overall: leave the car at P+R Nádraží Veleslavín or P+R Nádraží Holešovice and finish by Metro A or tram
On concert days expect temporary closures and traffic controls around the plateau — assume no parking nearby
parking.note: We deliberately do not publish tariffs or hour limits: zone rules and prices are updated by the city and change several times a year. Check the on-site signage or the official Prague parking zone map before you leave.

events.title: Events on Letenská pláň
events.body: Major open-air concerts, festivals and seasonal markets take place on Letenská pláň, the flat ground adjoining the park, rather than inside Letenské sady itself. Line-ups change weekly, so this site does not keep its own "what's on today" list — check the events calendar published by Prague City Tourism (prague.eu) or search Google Maps for "Letenská pláň" and open the latest updates there. During large events, sections of the plateau close, trams run crowded and noise carries across the whole hill.
events.linkText: Prague City Tourism — official events listing

route.title: Recommended Route
route.overview: Take the tram to Letenské náměstí — it avoids the climb — then cross Letenské sady to the viewpoint terrace, continue along the ridge to the Metronome, loop back past the Hanavský Pavilion and finish at the beer garden or the western edge of Letenská pláň for the evening light. The whole loop is roughly three kilometres on park paths and takes 60–90 minutes.
steps: Arrive at Letenské náměstí by tram and enter the park through the main alley
Walk straight to the viewpoint terrace above the retaining wall for the first panorama
Follow the ridge west and down towards the Metronome platform
Return along the lower path past the Hanavský Pavilion
Stop at the beer garden terrace — the same view with seating
Cross onto Letenská pláň for the wide, open horizon
Take the last half hour before sunset back on the viewpoint terrace
Walk downhill to Malá Strana or back to your tram
supplements: The route is mostly level; only the approach from Hradčanská metro involves a real climb
Wheelchair users and pushchairs can use the Letenské náměstí approach — it is step-free to the terrace
Paths are unpaved in places and can be muddy after rain
The exposed ridge is windy: bring a layer even in summer
Public toilets are available near the beer garden

spots.name: Metronome platform
spots.desc: Kinetic sculpture against the skyline; the moving arm adds motion blur after dark

photoSpots.tipsContent: The panorama is wide rather than vertical: a 24–70 mm covers the bridge group, and a short telephoto isolates the castle. Weekday mornings give the cleanest air and the fewest people. The park is inside controlled airspace for the city centre, so do not fly drones here.

stay.title: Where to stay near Letná Park
stay.intro: We do not recommend individual hotels — this is an independent guide and we cannot verify current operators. Instead, these are the areas that work best, with their real trade-offs:

areas.name: Letná & Holešovice (Prague 7)
areas.desc: Residential streets a few minutes from the park, with cafés and the tram at Letenské náměstí. Best if Letná is your main reason to visit.

areas.name: Malá Strana (Lesser Town)
areas.desc: Below the plateau beside the castle approach. Quiet and atmospheric; reaching the park means a 15–20 minute uphill walk.

areas.name: Old Town (Staré Město)
areas.desc: Everything within walking distance, but the busiest option. Two tram stops or a 20–30 minute walk to Letná.

areas.name: Along the Metro A corridor
areas.desc: Accommodation further out on line A reaches Hradčanská without changes — usually the best value if you are only on the hill for an evening.

stay.note: Compare current listings and prices on a booking platform of your choice — availability across Prague changes sharply during summer, Christmas markets and New Year.

items.question: What is the difference between Letná Park, Letenské sady and Letenská pláň?
items.answer: Letenské sady is the Czech name for the terraced park above the Vltava that most visitors call Letná Park. Letenská pláň is the large, flat open ground immediately west of it, used for sport, markets and open-air concerts. They sit next to each other on the same hill and are usually experienced as one area.

items.question: Is Letná Park free to enter?
items.answer: Yes. The park, promenades and viewpoint terrace are public and free at any hour of the day or night. You only pay for what you order at the beer garden or kiosks.

items.question: Which bank of the Vltava is Letná Park on?
items.answer: Letná Park is on the left bank of the Vltava, in Prague 7. It looks across the river towards the Old Town bridges, Petřín Hill and Prague Castle.

items.question: How do you get to Letná Park by tram or metro?
items.answer: By tram, take lines 1, 8, 12, 25 or 26 to Letenské náměstí, which is about a four-minute flat walk from the viewpoint terrace. By metro, take line A to Hradčanská and walk uphill through the park for about ten minutes, or use Malostranská for a shorter but steeper climb.

items.question: Where can I park near Letná Park?
items.answer: Street parking across Letná is mostly resident-priority blue zones with weekday enforcement, so it is not a reliable option. Use the paid car parks near the stadium and Letenské náměstí when they have space, or park at P+R Nádraží Veleslavín or P+R Nádraží Holešovice and finish by metro or tram.

items.question: What is the Metronome and why is it there?
items.answer: The Metronome is a kinetic sculpture by Vratislav Karel Novák installed in 1991. It stands on the plinth left behind by the Stalin Monument, which was unveiled in 1955 and demolished in 1962. It is not itself a Soviet-era monument.

items.question: Where is the best viewpoint in Letná Park?
items.answer: The paved terrace above the retaining wall, next to the beer garden, gives the classic panorama of the Vltava bridges. The Metronome platform offers a wider view of the river bend, and the western edge of Letenská pláň has the widest open horizon.

items.question: Is Letná Park suitable for wheelchairs and pushchairs?
items.answer: Yes, if you arrive by tram at Letenské náměstí: the route to the viewpoint terrace is step-free and mostly level. The approach from Hradčanská metro involves a noticeable climb, and some side paths are unpaved.

items.question: Are there events on Letenská pláň today?
items.answer: Major concerts and festivals are held on Letenská pláň, but programmes change weekly and we do not maintain a live calendar. Check the events listing published by Prague City Tourism on prague.eu, or open the Letenská pláň entry in Google Maps, before travelling.

officialManagement.title: Who looks after Letná Park
officialManagement.text:
Letenské sady is municipal green space in Prague 7, maintained by the city and open to the public free of charge. We are not the operator: this site is an independent visitor guide.

Practical consequences of that status: paths, lawns and terraces have no gate or closing time, events on Letenská pláň require separate permits from the city, and any changes to opening hours, tariffs or closures come from the city or the event organisers rather than from us. Always confirm details on the day of your visit.
